paper_title: TL;DR Too Long, Do Re-weighting for Effcient LLM Reasoning Compression
caption: Comparison of accuracy and generation length between Vanilla CoT and our method on four benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, AMC) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models. consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales.
model_annotation: The chart titled “DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B Comparison” illustrates a side-by-side comparison of accuracy between two methods, “Vanilla CoT” and “TLDR (Ours),” across four benchmark datasets. The horizontal axis contains the categorical datasets in left-to-right order GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC, with no apparent sorting beyond this sequence. The vertical axis is labeled “Accuracy (%)” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with major tick marks shown at regular 20-point intervals (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100). For each dataset, two adjacent bars are shown: a light/pale yellow bar for “Vanilla CoT” and a medium green bar for “TLDR (Ours),” as indicated by the legend at the top. On GSM8K, the Vanilla CoT bar reaches 89.4%, while the TLDR bar is slightly lower at approximately 87.7%, with a red annotation “-1.7%” above the green bar. On MATH500, the Vanilla CoT bar is 86.8% and the TLDR bar is approximately 87.4%, with a green “+0.6%” annotation. On AIME, the Vanilla CoT bar is 42.9% and the TLDR bar is approximately 41.2%, annotated in red as “-1.7%.” On AMC, the Vanilla CoT bar is 81.5% and the TLDR bar is approximately 83.1%, annotated in green as “+1.6%.” The only visible emphasis beyond color-coding is the per-category percentage-difference annotation placed above the green bars, with negative values in red and positive values in green.
